nodes.name: Settings
nodes.notes:
Every knob for the run lives here.

manifestSize must stay <= config('ingest.max_manifest') on the server (500).
uploadBatch bounds how many photos n8n holds in memory at once — raise it for a fast LAN, lower it if n8n starts swapping.

Move ingestToken to a credential before this workflow leaves your machine: values in a Set node are stored in plain text and travel with any export.

nodes.name: Extract archives
nodes.notes:
Unzipping happens in PowerShell, not in n8n's compression node: that node materialises every archive member as an in-memory binary item, which is fine for a dozen files and fatal for ten thousand.

Re-running is cheap — an archive whose timestamp has not moved is skipped.

nodes.name: Scan + hash
nodes.notes:
Emits NDJSON: one {name, sha256, bytes} per image.

The first run reads every byte on the NAS to hash it — for 10k photos expect tens of minutes. Every run after that reuses a path+size+mtime cache and finishes in seconds, which is what makes 'just run it again' a safe answer to a failed batch.

nodes.name: POST /ingest/plan
nodes.notes:
Names and hashes only — no image bytes.

This is the call that makes a 10k run survivable: it answers 'which of these do you not already have, and which SKU does each belong to' before a single photo crosses the wire. A re-run gets told 'all duplicates' for a few hundred KB of JSON.

nodes.name: Upload loop
nodes.notes:
Bounds memory. Without this, the read node would materialise every accepted photo as a binary item at once — 10k × 5 MB is not a thing n8n survives.

Set N8N_DEFAULT_BINARY_DATA_MODE=filesystem as well, so even one batch spills to disk instead of the heap.

nodes.name: POST /ingest/image
nodes.notes:
neverError + continueRegularOutput on purpose: one corrupt JPEG out of ten thousand must not abandon the other 9,999. Failures are counted in the summary instead.

The server re-hashes what actually arrived and refuses the row if it disagrees with sha256, so a truncated upload can never masquerade as a stored photo.

nodes.name: GET /ingest/report
nodes.notes: The catalogue's own account of the batch, read back from the database rather than inferred from HTTP responses. If these two disagree, trust this one.
